chapters.title: Inbox
chapters.summary: The inbox holds the decisions that need a person but are not a record to clean: merge decisions, golden record reviews, glossary reviews, value mapping matches, business exceptions, live SAP signals,

sections.text:
The inbox holds the decisions that need a person but are not a record to clean: merge decisions, golden record reviews, glossary reviews, value mapping matches, business exceptions, live SAP signals, and every change that waits for a second person. Fix work is where you clean failing records, and the only place you do; the inbox is where you answer everything else, closest to its deadline first.

Open it with the **Inbox** pill. The pill shows the number of open stewardship tasks.

sections.heading: The tabs
sections.text:
The page reads **Inbox** and has three tabs, each with a line that says what it holds:

- **Tasks**: fixes and matches waiting for a steward, and the business exceptions your exception rules raised. **Show** switches between **Queue tasks** and **Exceptions**.
- **Approvals**: fix batches and SAP write-backs that wait for a second person. Approve the ones you did not request.
- **SAP signals**: live signals from SAP, such as failed jobs and locked records.

You can link straight to exceptions as `/inbox?kind=exception`; it is also listed as **Inbox**, **Exceptions** for roles that approve or assign. The search is kept in the address (`?q=`), so a searched list can be shared or reloaded.

Exceptions also arrive from Fix work: **Raise an exception** on a failing record opens a tracked exception here, with its own owner and due date, for a record the team will not fix in this run.

What in the Inbox needs you most also appears on the [To do](/docs?page=todo) list, as approvals waiting and as items past their due time. The flag next to the bell opens it.

Failing SAP records are not worked here. The old **Issues** tab moved to Fix work: `/inbox?kind=issues` opens [Fix work](/docs?page=fix) on your own records (**Mine**), where the record panel offers **Take it**, **Assign to**, **Accept risk**, **Not an issue** and **Fixed in SAP**.

sections.heading: Tasks
sections.text:
The **When** filter shows how many tasks are **Overdue** and **Due in 24 hours**. When the queue holds more than the page loaded, a notice says how many are loaded. To see who holds the work across all queues, open **Insights › Operate**.

Filter the list with:

- **Who**: **Everyone**, **Mine** or **Unassigned**, each with its count.
- **When**: **Any time**, **Overdue**, **Due in 24 hours** or **Escalated**.
- **Type**: one task type, or **All types**.
- **Priority**, when the tasks differ. Priority 1 is the highest.
- **Search**: the task, record, object, type or assignee.

The list is on the left, with an SLA pill on each row such as "Due in 5h" or "2d overdue". Each row is titled by what it decides and its object, such as "Merge decision in Material master"; an exception is titled by its check, such as "Custom Rule: Blank material group in Material master", never a bare "Exception". The line under the title reads in short sentences: who holds it, its priority and how long ago it was raised. The selected task is on the right: the record, object, priority, status, assignee, age and due time, any suggested decision with its confidence, and **Open record**.

### How to work a task

1. Pick a view, for example **Mine**, or **Overdue** under **When**.
2. Select a task, or move with `j` and `k`.
3. Read the detail, and select **Open record** if you need the record itself.
4. Select **Approve**, or **Reject** and write why in **Reason**. **Keep task open** backs out. The reason is kept on the task and helps Meridian suggest better next time.
5. **Claim** makes the task yours. **Escalate** raises its priority and marks it escalated.

What approval does depends on the type: a merge decision merges the two master records, a golden record review promotes the record, a glossary review marks the term reviewed, and a value mapping match confirms the mapping. A rejected merge is recorded as "do not match" and not proposed again.

To act on several, tick them and choose **Claim**, **Approve**, **Reject with reason** or **Escalate**. Approving and rejecting need the approve permission.

sections.heading: Exceptions
sections.text: Choose **Show**, **Exceptions** on the Tasks tab. Exceptions are sorted by deadline. Each shows its title, category, status, assignee and severity. Select one to read its source and estimated impact, then **Resolve** (with notes on what was done), **Claim** or **Escalate**. Escalating moves it up one tier with a shorter deadline. Tick several to **Claim**, **Escalate** or **Resolve with notes** together. Roles that manage rules see **Manage exception rules**, where each rule is switched on or off and new ones are added.

sections.heading: SAP signals
sections.text: **SAP signals** lists signals by category, severity, status, source and time raised; select **Review** to read one.

sections.heading: Approvals
sections.text:
**Approvals** is the one place where a second person approves a change. It is the data owner's landing page.

- **Fix batches**: the values decided in Fix work, by batch. Each row names the rules it fixes, who requested it, how many records it holds and its first change, such as `MARA.MATKL` on `MATNR=1`: blank to `001`. **Show** filters **Waiting for approval** (the default), **Approved**, **Exported** or **All**. Select a batch to read every item and the before and after, then **Approve batch**. The person who drafted a batch cannot approve it.
- **SAP write-backs**: live write-back requests with the rule, the run, the records, who requested them and when. You cannot approve a request you made. When live write-back is off for the deployment, the card says so: export fixes from a batch and load them in SAP instead.

Approving needs the approve permission. Auditors (view audit) read the fix batches here as four-eyes evidence, without approving. Exporting an approved batch stays in Fix work, under **Batches and export** (see [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals)).

sections.heading: Service levels
sections.text: Each item has a due time, set directly or worked out from its SLA hours. It is at risk once less than half its window remains and overdue once the time passes. Meridian sends one notification for each event (at risk, not acknowledged, breached), and copies the team lead on the last two. Teams and SLA policies are set under **Settings**, **Triage** (see [Administration](/docs?page=admin)).

sections.heading: Keys and notifications
sections.text: On the list, `j` and `k` move, `Enter` opens the record, `a` claims the item, `r` approves (or opens resolve on an exception), `x` rejects with a reason, and `Escape` closes the panel. The bell in the index bar shows your unread notifications; **Open all** goes to the full list at [/inbox/notifications](/inbox/notifications).

chapters.title: Analysis
chapters.summary: The **Analysis** section of the **More** menu holds the pages for understanding the data rather than cleaning it: the Home overview, the Insights views and their reports, What-if, Runs, and the as-is

sections.text: The **Analysis** section of the **More** menu holds the pages for understanding the data rather than cleaning it: the Home overview, the Insights views and their reports, What-if, Runs, and the as-is processes. Leads, analysts and data owners use them most. Every page follows the run in the scope bar.

sections.heading: Home
sections.text:
**Home** answers how healthy your SAP data is and what to do next. Each role lands on its own version: the data lead page, the Basis page or the process page. Stewards land on Fix work instead, and can still open the steward Home with **View as**, **Steward**. **View as** changes the layout only, never your rights.

The page shows the score on its ruler with the verdict (**Go**, **At risk** or **No-go**) and any cap, the object map, the four sentences (**Situation**, **What changed**, **Why it matters**, **Do next**), the objects holding the score back, and your own work. On the data lead page, **Root causes**, **S/4 migration** and **Cleansing opportunity** follow, each for the same scope. They came from the old Insights overview, which repeated Home and now opens Home. **Run analysis** opens a panel to extract and analyse a system's objects, for roles that may start extractions. From anywhere, press Ctrl K (⌘K) and then Ctrl 1 (⌘1) to go Home.

sections.heading: Insights
sections.text:
**Insights** turns findings into answers for the people who decide. Its views, listed under **Insights** in the **More** menu, each have tabs under the title:

- **Summary**: the **Executive summary** and **Reports**, the report library with the board pack, analyst workbook, run comparison, object and owner reports, each with a preview and **Download**.
- **Progress**: the burn-down page, which ends with a **Team** section (see [Progress](/docs?page=progress)), **Trends**, which re-scores one system's runs under today's weights so the line compares like with like, and **Forecast**, which projects each object's score 7, 30 and 90 days ahead once there are runs on three different days.
- **Explore**: **Failing rules** grouped by rule, object, field, dimension or severity and ranked by impact; **Value at risk** for priced SAP features; **Lineage**, which also lists the **Relationships** the miner found between fields; **Patterns**, whose **Anomalies** tab lists values far outside the usual range; and **Duplicates**, where you create merge proposals from a cluster.
- **Readiness**: **Waves**, a grid of objects against migration waves, and **Processes**, the readiness of each procure to pay or order to cash step.
- **Operate**: **Owners**, the score and open work per owner with their digest. How the cleaning team keeps up (capacity, queue age and bottlenecks) is the **Team** section of Progress.

Every Insights page has the same build: the header with **Export** and **Present**, the four sentences, then the ledger that ranks the work and the charts. Select a rule in a ledger to open the finding beside the page, with what failed, how many, why, the samples and the fix.

sections.heading: What-if
sections.text: **What-if** applies every rule fix to a copy of a run and compares the score before and after. Nothing is written anywhere. Choose the **Analysis run**, select **Run simulation**, and read **Score before**, **Score after**, **Findings resolved**, **Findings introduced**, **Cells changed** and **Records fixed**, then the rules the fixes change and their side effects. **Create fix batch from this simulation** turns the result into a draft batch. What-if appears for roles with apply or approve; simulating needs the analyse permission.

sections.heading: Runs
sections.text:
**Runs** lists every run, newest first, with its status, score and critical and high findings, each against the previous run of its lineage. From here you can:

- Tick two runs and press `c`, or use **Compare with previous** on a run's page, to see which rules and records were fixed or newly fail.
- Open a run to read its objects, findings, steps and configuration. **Re-run analysis** checks the stored data again with today's rules.
- **Rename** a run, **Pin as baseline** (the reference that later runs of the object are compared with, see [Monitoring](/docs?page=monitoring)), and archive older runs.

Pinning and archiving need the analyse permission.

sections.heading: As-is processes and discovery runs
sections.text: **As-is processes** reconstructs your real processes from SAP documents, level 1 to level 5, and measures them against a reference. Each process shows its coverage, fitness, variants, cases, median duration and the data quality defects on the objects it touches. Open one to read its **Flow**, **BPMN** diagram, **Variants**, **Conformance** and **Reference**. **Discovery runs** lists each discovery job with its stages and the SAP tables it read. Running discovery and exporting models need the process permissions.

sections.heading: Ask Meridian
sections.text: The **Ask Meridian** button at the bottom right of every page answers short questions in plain words, such as "Which objects are weakest?" or "What changed since the last run?", from your run's figures, with a link to the page behind each answer.

chapters.title: Master data
chapters.summary: Master data management brings together records that describe the same real thing, such as one supplier held twice, and keeps one trusted version of it: the golden record. Stewards review matches and m

sections.text:
Master data management brings together records that describe the same real thing, such as one supplier held twice, and keeps one trusted version of it: the golden record. Stewards review matches and merges here; data owners see how healthy their master data is.

Open **More**, **Master data**: **Overview**, **Survivorship**, **Golden records**, **Glossary** and **Match rules**. Every role can read these pages.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The [overview](/mdm) shows **MDM health** out of 100: **Healthy** at 85 or more, **Needs attention** from 60 and **Unhealthy** below. Four inputs make it up, each with a small trend line:

- **Coverage** (40%): the share of SAP objects with a promoted golden record.
- **Match confidence** (30%): the average confidence of automatically merged records.
- **Steward SLA** (20%): the share of stewardship tasks resolved within their SLA.
- **Source consistency** (10%): the share of fields where every source agrees with the golden record.

**Health over time** charts the score, and **Match work** lists the open stewardship tasks, merge decisions first, each opening the [Inbox](/docs?page=inbox).

sections.heading: Golden records
sections.text:
[Golden records](/mdm/golden) lists each record with its SAP key, object, status, sources, confidence and open issues. A status is **Candidate** (assembled, not confirmed), **Pending review**, **Golden** (the trusted version) or **Superseded** (merged into another record). Filter by **Domain**, **Status** and confidence.

### How to review a golden record

1. Open a record. Read its status and confidence on **Overview**.
2. Check **Golden fields**: one grid with a row per field and a column per source (a column per merged record once records are merged). The value the golden record kept is highlighted, and **Chosen by** says why in words, such as "Source priority from PRD", with the record key or upload label beside it. Approvers can **Override** a field there, with a reason.
3. Select **Promote** to make it golden. The merged values replace the current golden fields, and this cannot be undone. Promoting needs the approve permission.

**Related**, **History** and **Audit** list linked records, each change and every logged action.

sections.heading: Duplicates and merging
sections.text:
The match rules find candidate pairs. Every pair is decided in **Master data**, [**Match review**](/mdm/golden/merge): the pairs are listed on the left, and the selected pair is shown on the right with the two records side by side, the fields that differ highlighted and the identical ones folded away. Give a reason, then select **Merge**, **Not a match** or **Skip**; the next pair opens on its own. On the keyboard, **j** and **k** move between pairs, **m** merges, **n** marks not a match and **s** skips (without a reason, **m** and **n** put you in the reason box; press Ctrl Enter, or ⌘ Enter on a Mac, to send). Merging and marking not a match need the approve permission.

Pairs also reach you from:

- **Match review**: every duplicate pair, from the match rules and the cleaning engine, compared field by field; keep one or mark it not a match. Old links to Fix work's Duplicates tab open it.
- **Insights**, **Explore**, **Duplicates**: pick an object and a record, see its cluster, choose the surviving record and select **Create merge proposal**. Below it are the matcher's **Scored pairs** and the miner's **Likely duplicates**; **Review** on a likely duplicate opens it in Match review. Anomalies are under **Patterns** and field relationships under **Lineage**.
- The [Inbox](/docs?page=inbox): each merge decision waits there. Approving keeps the record with the higher confidence, fills its blank fields from the other and marks the other **Superseded**. Rejecting records the pair as "do not match".

Creating merge proposals and merging need the approve permission.

sections.heading: Match rules
sections.text:
[Match rules](/mdm/match-rules) has three tabs:

- **Rules**: each rule compares one field (**Exact**, **Fuzzy**, **Phonetic**, **Numeric range** or **Semantic**) with a weight and a threshold. **Simulate** shows the candidate pairs and how many would auto-merge, be dismissed or go to a steward.
- **Tuning**: a dry run that re-scores the newest stored pairs with the weights and thresholds you enter. Pairs at or above **Auto-merge at** merge on their own, pairs between **Review floor** and that point go to a steward, and pairs below are dismissed. Nothing is saved.
- **Constraints**: pairs pinned as **Do not match** or **Always match**, created when a steward accepts, rejects or unmerges a pair.

Editing rules needs the manage rules permission.

sections.heading: Survivorship
sections.text: When sources disagree, [survivorship](/mdm/survivorship) decides which value the golden record keeps, field by field: for example the most recent, the most complete or a trusted system. **Set by** shows whether a person or the model suggested the rule; a suggested rule takes effect only once a person activates it. Until a field has a rule, the most recent source value wins.

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.text: The [glossary](/mdm/glossary) defines each business term, where it lives in SAP and who owns it, with its approved values and the rules that check it. Terms are drafted from the fields Meridian's rules check. Open a term to edit its **Business definition**, ask for an **Auto-draft**, or select **Mark reviewed** when it is due.

chapters.title: Rules
chapters.summary: Rules are the checks Meridian runs on your SAP data. Every score, failing record and suggested value comes from a deterministic rule, never from a guess. Stewards use these pages to see what is checke

sections.text:
Rules are the checks Meridian runs on your SAP data. Every score, failing record and suggested value comes from a deterministic rule, never from a guess. Stewards use these pages to see what is checked, why a record fails and to write new rules; administrators set how the score is weighted and when alerts go out.

Open **More**, **Rules**. The section holds **Rules**, **Contracts**, **Drafts**, **Data dictionary** and **Scoring**. Who is told about what lives under **Admin**, **Alerts**.

sections.heading: The rules list
sections.text:
The [Rules](/rules) page counts your rules and how many are enabled, and has three tabs: **All**, **Suppressions** and **Feedback**.

- **All** shows the figures **Failing**, **Disabled** and **Not run yet**, a filter bar (search, system, check type, dimension, severity, state, source, object and table), and the ledger **Rules, lowest pass rate first**. A rule that does not apply to your loaded configuration reads "Not applicable"; hover it for the reason. **Coverage by object** shows, for each object, how many rules apply on your loaded configuration and how many do not; it is measured on a finished run, so it stays empty until the first run completes.
- **Suppressions** lists rules or single records kept out of the score until a date, with the reason and who made it.
- **Feedback** shows, per rule, the records stewards flagged and the false-positive rate. A rate over 30% is marked red.

sections.heading: A rule's page
sections.text: Open a rule to see its last pass rate, its description, where it applies on each system and why, the fields and tables it reads, its owner and steward, its versions, a line of its pass rate over runs, **What changed between versions**, and its conditions, written as the check on the SAP field, such as "Required value on `LFA1.STCD1`". **See failing records** opens its records. The message and instruction you read in the Fix work record panel come from here.

sections.heading: How to enable or disable a rule
sections.text: Flip the switch in the **State** column, or open the rule and select **Disable rule**. A message offers **Undo**. The change applies from the next run; past runs keep their results.

sections.heading: How to write a new rule
sections.text:
1. Select **New rule**.
2. Choose the **Object** and a **Check type**: Required value, Allowed values, Pattern match, Field-to-field consistency, Dependency check or No duplicates.
3. Fill in the SAP `TABLE.FIELD` names, the **Message**, the **Severity** and the **Dimension**.
4. Choose a run under **Dry run against** and select **Dry run** to see how many records are checked and failing, with samples.
5. Select **Save rule**. It is enabled only after a clean dry run.

**Drafts** holds rules being written. You can describe a rule in words and select **Generate with AI**; the model sees field metadata and counts only, never record values. **Publish rule** makes a saved draft active from the next run.

sections.heading: Learned rules
sections.text: **Learned from your data** lists patterns your own data follows for at least 95% of records, such as a field decided by another field. **Approve** turns a pattern into an active rule at medium severity; **Reject** drops it.

sections.heading: Contracts and the data dictionary
sections.text: A data contract turns rules into a promise between a producer and a consumer system, checked after every run and marked compliant or not. A draft is submitted for approval, then activated by someone other than its author. The data dictionary looks up standard SAP fields by `TABLE.FIELD` and finds the rules on each.

sections.heading: Versions and what changed
sections.text: Every change to a rule makes a new version, and a new version applies from the next analysis run; past runs keep the result they had. On a rule's page, **What changed between versions** compares a version with the one before it, or with the rule as shipped when it is the first change. Choose the version under **Version to read**. Lines that were added and removed are listed, so you can see exactly which threshold, field or message moved. When two versions read the same, the page says **Nothing differs**. The author of a version cannot approve it.

sections.heading: Scoring
sections.text: [Scoring](/rules/scoring) is about how the score is made. It sets the dimension weights (they must sum to 1.00; **Use DAMA defaults** restores 0.25, 0.25, 0.20, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10), the score bands that decide Go, At risk and No-go, the planner assumptions and the cost model behind value at risk. A preview shows how the current score would change before you save. Saving needs the manage settings permission; others read the page.

sections.heading: Alerts
sections.text: Telling people is a separate page: [Alerts](/admin/alerts), under **Admin**. It holds the thresholds that raise an alert (critical or high failing rules, or a score that drops by more than a set number of points), a score floor per object, the channels that carry alerts and digests (email, Slack, Teams or a signed webhook) and the default digest. Scoring answers "how good is the data"; Alerts answers "who is told, and when". See [Administration](/docs?page=admin).

sections.heading: Who can change what
sections.text:
- Writing, enabling and publishing rules and creating contracts need the manage rules permission (Platform admin, Data steward).
- Approving learned rules, activating contracts and creating suppressions need the approve permission. The author of a rule version cannot approve it.
- Exporting the rule list needs the export permission.

chapters.title: Data in
chapters.summary: Everything Meridian checks has to come in first: from a connected SAP system, from an export file, or as part of a migration wave. The **Data in** section of the **More** menu holds the three pages fo

sections.text: Everything Meridian checks has to come in first: from a connected SAP system, from an export file, or as part of a migration wave. The **Data in** section of the **More** menu holds the three pages for that: **Systems**, **Import file** and **Migration**. SAP Basis teams and analysts use them most; stewards rarely need them.

sections.heading: Systems
sections.text:
[Systems](/systems) lists every connected system with its type, health (**Healthy**, **Degraded**, **Unreachable**, **Sign-in refused** or **Not tested**), the objects that hold data, the latest score, whether its configuration is loaded, and when data was last read. In the **More** menu the entry carries a dot for the worst health: red when a system cannot be reached or refused sign-in, amber when one is degraded, green when all are healthy.

### How to connect a system

1. Select **Connect system**, enter a **Name** such as "PRD ECC", and choose the **Type** and **Environment**.
2. Fill in the connection fields. ECC, S/4HANA on premise and Extended Warehouse Management connect over RFC with host, client, instance number, user and password; the SAP user needs read authorisations only. S/4HANA Cloud, BTP, SuccessFactors and Concur connect with OAuth: base URL, client ID and client secret, and a token URL where asked.
3. Select **Connect system**, then **Test connection**. Meridian also checks every connection every 30 minutes.

Connecting and editing systems needs a role that manages systems, such as SAP Basis or a programme lead.

### If the SAP RFC library is not installed

A system that connects over RFC (ECC, S/4HANA on premise, Extended Warehouse Management) shows **Unreachable** with the reason "SAP RFC library not installed on the server" until the SAP NW RFC SDK is built into Meridian's images. The licence for the SDK stays with you, so Meridian does not ship it. On the host that runs Meridian, run `sudo bash scripts/build-rfc-overlay.sh --sdk /usr/local/sap/nwrfcsdk` (change the path to where you unpacked the SDK). It builds the API and worker images with the library and restarts them from an overlay file that updates keep. Then open the system and select **Test connection**. **Extract** stays off until the library is there. Importing a file works without it.

### How to load configuration

On the system's **Health** tab, select **Load configuration**. It tells Meridian which fields and rules apply to this system; until it loads, every rule applies by default. "Configuration loaded with gaps" means some areas could not be read, and **Try again** retries.

### How to run an extraction

1. Open the system and select **Extract**.
2. Tick the objects to read, and set the scope: company codes, plants, sales or purchasing organisations, and a document date window for transactional objects. Leave a field empty to read all.
3. Give the run a **Run label** if you like, then select **Extract N objects**, or **Extract and analyse** to score the data as soon as it is read, and **Confirm**.

When the analysis finishes, the run's work list is built and its failing records appear in [Fix work](/docs?page=fix). **Extraction log** on the **Runs** tab shows each step, its duration and any error.

### How to schedule re-evaluation

On the **Health** tab, under **Scheduled re-evaluation**, choose an object, a schedule (daily, weekly, monthly, hourly or your own) and an extraction mode, then **Add schedule**. **Full download** reads every record; **Changes only** re-reads the records SAP's change log shows as changed, with a full download at least weekly. The next run after an export is what confirms your fixes, so a schedule keeps Fix work and Progress current.

sections.heading: Import file
sections.text:
Use [Import file](/import) when you have an export but no live connection. Importing needs the upload permission.

1. Select **Choose file**, or drop one on the page: CSV, TSV, TXT, XLSX, XLS, JSON or Parquet, up to 2 GB.
2. Meridian says what the file looks like, such as "looks like Material master (92% sure)". Check the object and the **Column mapping**: each of your columns, the standard field it maps to and the confidence.
3. Select **Run import**, and follow the steps from reading the file to scoring.
4. Select **Open the run**.

Each import becomes a run. Imports of the same objects are compared with each other, so a second file of the same data confirms the fixes of the first. A required field with no column is named, and the checks that need it are skipped; an administrator can map the column under **Field mapping**.

sections.heading: Migration
sections.text:
[Migration](/migration) tells you whether your data is ready to move to S/4HANA, wave by wave. It shows to roles with the analyse permission.

- **Create wave**: a name, source and target system, the modules, a target date, a stage (**Plan**, **Mock 1**, **Mock 2**, **Dress rehearsal** or **Cutover**) and a **Minimum readiness %**, 95 by default.
- **Run now** scores every module of the wave. Readiness is the share of records that would load; a record is blocked by a critical or high gap. A module is **Go** with nothing blocked, **At risk** with readiness at 90% or more, and **No-go** otherwise. The wave takes the worst verdict of its modules.
- **Dry run (S/4 load)** applies the target's load checks to your source records and lists each record that would fail to load, with the reasons. Nothing is written to SAP.
- On a wave's **Blockers** tab, **Create fix batch** drafts a batch for one object, gap and field, which is then approved and exported as in [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals).
- When the verdict is **Go**, **Sign off** records who signed off and when. It needs the approve permission.

chapters.title: Administration
chapters.summary: The admin pages are where the people who run Meridian manage access, routing, alerts, retention, the language model and the installation. Open **More**, **Admin**. You see only the pages your role all

sections.text:
The admin pages are where the people who run Meridian manage access, routing, alerts, retention, the language model and the installation. Open **More**, **Admin**. You see only the pages your role allows; a page opened without the right permission says which one it needs, such as "Needs the `manage_users` permission".

The admin pages share one row of tabs under the page title: **Overview** (Settings, with the checklist of what still needs setting up), **Users**, **Roles and access**, **Sign-in**, **Alerts**, **Triage**, **Field mapping**, **Reference data**, **Jobs**, **Audit log**, **Billing** and **Licence**. A tab appears only when your role may open it, so the row is the same on every admin page, and you can move from one to the next without going back to **More**. When the right-hand side of the index bar shows a number on the **To do** flag, admin chores such as access requests, pending invitations, seats and expiring grants are in it; see [To do](/docs?page=todo).

sections.heading: Users
sections.text:
This page needs `manage_users`. The header counts the people, how many never signed in and how many seats the licence has used, such as "41 of 50 seats". The list shows each person's role, **Status**, last sign-in and member-since date. Filter by **Search**, **Status**, role and system; the filters are part of the address, so you can share a filtered list.

### User statuses

- **Invited**: the invitation was sent and has not been accepted. It works for seven days.
- **Invite expired**: seven days passed without the person setting a password. Resend the invite.
- **Active**: the person can sign in. **Password change due** next to it means they must choose a new password at their next sign-in.
- **Locked**: ten failed sign-ins locked the account for fifteen minutes. It unlocks by itself, or you can reset the password.
- **Suspended**: the person cannot sign in. Their name stays on past work.

### How to invite a user

1. Select **Invite user** and enter the **Email** and, if you like, a **Name**.
2. Choose a **Role**, or add access for one system or object, with an optional **Expires** date. Add at least one.
3. Select **Send invitation**. The person sets a password on the **Join Meridian** page, or signs in with single sign-on if you turned it on.

An invited person takes a seat at once. When seats are nearly used up the page warns you, and at the limit invitations are refused until you suspend someone or raise the licence.

### Invitations that need attention

When invitations are older than seven days or an email could not be delivered, a notice says so. Open the row's actions to **Resend invite**, **Copy invite link** (a one-time link you can pass on yourself when email does not arrive, which works until the date shown) or **Revoke invite**. Revoking removes the person from the list; you can invite them again later.

### How to import many people

Select **Import users** to add a team from a CSV file. Paste it or choose **Upload a CSV file**. The columns are `email`, `name`, `role`, `system` and `module`; the last two may be blank. Select **Check the file** first: every line gets a verdict, and the page shows how many seats the lines need against how many are free. Nothing is written until you select **Import**. Lines that fail are skipped and named, and the rest are invited. A file can be up to 256 KB, and the import is refused as a whole when it would pass the seat limit.

### How to change, suspend or remove a user

Select the user to change the role or access. In the row's actions you can **Suspend** (the person cannot sign in, their history stays), **Reactivate**, **Reset password** (sends a reset email) or **Remove**. Select several rows to suspend, reactivate, resend or reset in one step; anyone the system refuses, such as yourself or the last administrator, is skipped and named. **Remove** asks for confirmation. A user referenced by audit or stewardship records cannot be removed, so suspend them instead. **Export users** downloads the list.

For the fix workflow, give each steward the Data steward role and each approver the Data owner role, so every batch has a second person who can approve it. See [Roles and access](/docs?page=roles).

sections.heading: Roles and access
sections.text:
**Roles and access** controls what each role can do and where. It has the tabs **Roles**, **Matrix**, **Users & scopes**, **Requests**, **History**, **Invite** and **API keys**. Built-in roles are read only: **Clone** one, then tick or clear permissions in its grid and **Save permissions**. The **Matrix** shows what every role may do on each kind of data, and the **What this role sees** preview lists the pages a person holding only that role could open, without impersonating anyone. On **Users & scopes**, add grants by system and module, give a grant an expiry date and check a user's **Effective permissions**. Before a grant is saved, a preview shows what it changes. **Expiring within 30 days** lists the grants to review. **Requests** lists the access requests people sent with **Request access**: **Grant** or **Decline** each. **History** lists every change. The details are in [Roles and access](/docs?page=roles).

### API keys

An API key lets another system, such as your scheduler or reporting tool, call Meridian without a person signing in. Open **Roles and access**, then **API keys**.

- **Create a key**: name it, choose what it may do (the same roles and scopes as a person, never an administrator role) and, if you like, when it expires. The key is shown once. Copy it into the other system straight away; Meridian keeps only a fingerprint of it.
- **Revoke a key** to stop it working at once. **Delete** removes it from the list.
- A key belongs to a service account. Service accounts are not people: they do not use a seat, cannot sign in with a password and are managed only here.
- Keys that expire within 14 days appear in **To do** for administrators.

sections.heading: Audit log
sections.text: The **Audit log** records who did what, with **When**, **Who**, **Action** and **Request**, and exports as `.xlsx` or `.csv`. **AI audit** lists every call to the language model with its outcome. Every decision in Fix work, every approval and every export is in the log. Admins, programme leads and auditors can open it.

sections.heading: Settings
sections.text: **Overview**, the Settings page, shows the deployment (tenant, licence and language model), then **Alert channels**, **Retention** (how long runs, reports and audit rows are kept; only archived runs are ever purged, never a baseline) and **Health checks** for the database, Redis, object storage, the language model, the licence server and migrations, with **Check again**.

sections.heading: Alerts
sections.text:
[Alerts](/admin/alerts) answers who is told about what, and when. It needs `manage_settings`; others read it.

- **When to alert**: alert when a run has at least this many critical or high failing rules, or when an object's score falls by more than a set number of points against the previous run. **Score floors per object** raise an in-app alert when an analysis scores an object below its floor. Select **Save thresholds**.
- **Channels**: Email, Slack, Microsoft Teams or a signed webhook. Select **Add channel**, choose the type, enter the address or an `https` URL, and choose a digest: **Daily digest**, **Weekly digest**, **No digest**, or **Send new critical findings immediately**. A **Board pack** channel receives the board pack and the analyst workbook for the latest finished run, weekly or monthly. Then **Send test**. Alerts carry counts, rule IDs and links, never record values. A channel with no digest and no immediate delivery never fires.
- **Default digest**: the summary the whole organisation gets by default, by email and Teams. Each person still picks their own under **Your own digest**.

How the score itself is weighted is a different page: see **Scoring** in [Rules](/docs?page=rules).

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.text:
[Sign-in](/admin/sign-in) needs `manage_users`. It holds three things.

- **Single sign-on**: connect your identity provider through OpenID Connect, such as Microsoft Entra ID or Okta. Enter a **Display name**, the **Issuer address**, the **Client ID** and the **Client secret** (it is stored but never shown again), and optionally the **Allowed email domains**. Register the redirect address the page shows at your identity provider, then test the connection before you save. A person who signs in this way for the first time becomes a viewer with no access grants; give access afterwards under Roles and access. **Turn off single sign-on** removes the settings; people keep their accounts and sign in with a password, or use **Forgot password**.
- **Require single sign-on**: password sign-in then stops for everyone except administrators, so a person who cannot reach the identity provider is locked out until an administrator changes this. Meridian asks you to confirm.
- **Password sign-in**: the rules are fixed and are not settings. A password has at least 12 characters, is not the email name and is not a common password. Ten failed sign-ins lock an account for 15 minutes.

sections.heading: Triage
sections.text:
**Triage** decides who gets new issues and how long they have, which drives the **Overdue** and **Due today** pills in Fix work and the SLA pills in the Inbox.

1. Under **Teams**, add a team with a name, a strategy (**Round robin** or **Least loaded**), a lead and members.
2. Under **Assignment rules**, add rules that send issues by severity, module, rule, dimension, company code, plant or sales organisation to a team or person. The first match wins; anything else goes to the fallback user.
3. Under **SLA policies**, set the acknowledge and resolve times and the at-risk share.
4. Under **Working calendar**, set the time zone, work days, hours, fallback user and holidays.

sections.heading: Field mapping
sections.text: **Field mapping** tells Meridian which column of an imported file holds each standard field. Type the file's header in **Customer column** and **Save**. A standard field with no column is skipped by every check that needs it.

sections.heading: Language model
sections.text: Meridian runs its own language model inside the installation to write narrative and remediation text. It is set when Meridian is installed and has no settings page. It never sees SAP data: it receives aggregated finding summaries only, and every score, count and suggested value comes from deterministic checks. The **AI audit** tab of the audit log lists every call it answered.

sections.heading: Jobs, reference data and licence
sections.text: **Jobs** lists extractions, analyses, uploads and simulations with their status and any error. **Reference data** shows the postal code and BIC lists held per system. **Licence** shows the tier, seats, modules and renewal date, and, for platform admins, the version running with **Update now** when a new one is out. The update restarts Meridian for everyone and rolls back on its own if a step fails. From the server, `sudo bash scripts/update.sh` updates and `sudo bash scripts/update.sh --rollback` returns to the previous version.

chapters.title: Keyboard shortcuts and search
chapters.summary: Cleaning data is repetitive, so Meridian can be driven from the keyboard: you can work a whole list of records without touching the mouse. This chapter lists every key and explains the two search boxe

sections.text:
Cleaning data is repetitive, so Meridian can be driven from the keyboard: you can work a whole list of records without touching the mouse. This chapter lists every key and explains the two search boxes. Keys never fire while you are typing in a box, a list or a text area, or while a dialog is open, and they ignore Ctrl, ⌘ and Alt unless stated. On Windows and Linux, read ⌘ as Ctrl.

Press `?` on any page, or choose **Keyboard shortcuts** in the help menu, to see the list for the page you are on.

sections.heading: Everywhere
sections.text:
- `/`: open the search (the same as `Ctrl+K`), where typing a record key or name lists the failing records it matches.
- Ctrl K (⌘K): open **Search or jump to...**, for any page, object, rule or record key.
- `?`: show the keyboard shortcuts.
- Ctrl 1 (⌘1), with **Search or jump to...** open: go to your Home page. Outside it, Ctrl or ⌘ with a number is left to your browser for switching tabs.
- `Escape`: close the **More** menu, a dialog, a side panel or a guided tour.

sections.heading: Fix work
sections.text:
On the **Records to fix** tab:

- `j` or the Down arrow: next record.
- `k` or the Up arrow: previous record.
- `a`: accept the record's suggested values. They go into your draft fix batch, and the next record comes up.
- `t`: take the record, so it is assigned to you.
- `u`: undo the record's proposed values.
- `Enter`: open the full record.

`a` and `u` need the apply permission and `t` the assign permission. The keys are printed under the list as a reminder.

sections.heading: Objects
sections.text:
On an object's page:

- `1` to `5`: open **Records to fix**, **Overview**, **Rules**, **Fields** and **Records by rule**.
- On **Records to fix**, `j` and `k` (or the arrow keys) move between records and `Enter` opens the full record.
- `f`: open the full record of the row the keyboard is on in a rule's record list, or of the first record.

sections.heading: Inbox
sections.text:
- `j` and `k`: next or previous item.
- `Enter`: open the record behind the item.
- `a`: claim the item.
- `r`: approve the task, or open the resolve box on an exception.
- `x`: reject the task with a reason.
- `Escape`: close the panel.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
When a table has the focus (select a row, or press Tab until it is outlined):

- Up and Down arrows: move between rows. Home and End: first or last row.
- `Enter`: open the focused row. Space: select it, where the table allows.
- `Escape`: clear the selection.

On **Runs**, with two runs ticked, `c` opens their comparison.

sections.heading: Finding a record
sections.text:
The search in the top bar finds records as well as pages. It searches the failing records of the run you are viewing.

1. Press `/`, or select **Search or jump to...**.
2. Type at least two characters of a record key or a name, such as a material number or a vendor name.
3. Move through the matches under **Records** with the arrow keys. Each shows its name or key, its object and its issue count.
4. Press `Enter` to open the record in its object, on **Records to fix**, with the record picked. `Escape` closes the search.

Only records that fail a check in the run are listed. To find a record that passes, open the object and use its search, or the search page below.

sections.heading: Search or jump
The search page
sections.text: The search page at [/search](/search) lists objects, rules, glossary terms, batches and runs that match your text, exact matches first. Select a row to open it. With the export permission, **Export** downloads the findings.

chapters.title: Troubleshooting
chapters.summary: This chapter lists the problems people meet most often in Meridian, the message you see and what to do. The fix work problems come first. Some fixes need an administrator; each section says so.

sections.text: This chapter lists the problems people meet most often in Meridian, the message you see and what to do. The fix work problems come first. Some fixes need an administrator; each section says so.

sections.heading: No finished run yet
sections.text:
Fix work reads "No finished run yet" and Progress reads "Nothing to track yet" when no run has finished analysing.

1. Open **More**, **Analysis**, **Runs** to see whether a run is still going.
2. If there is no run at all, connect a system under **Data in**, **Systems**, or load a file with **Import file** (see [Data in](/docs?page=data-in)).
3. If a colleague sees records you do not, your access may be scoped to some systems or objects. Ask an administrator to check your grants.

sections.heading: The work list is not built for this run
sections.text:
Fix work reads "This run's work list is not built yet", and an object's **Records to fix** tab reads "The work list for this run is not built yet". Runs analysed before the work list existed, or whose build failed, have none.

1. If your role can run analyses, select **Build the work list**. It takes a few minutes for a large run; the records appear when it finishes.
2. Otherwise, ask an analyst or a steward to build it. Until then the object's **Overview** and **Rules** tabs show what fails.
3. Or choose a newer run in the scope bar: every new run builds its work list as part of the analysis.

sections.heading: I cannot see Fix work
sections.text:
The **Fix work** pill appears only for roles that can apply fixes or approve them: Platform admin, Programme lead, Data steward and Data owner. An analyst, Basis administrator, auditor or viewer does not see it.

- You can still open any object's **Records to fix** tab and read each record. The panel says "Your role can view this record. Fixing it needs the apply permission."
- Ask an administrator for the Data steward role, or use **Request access** where a button offers it. See [Roles and access](/docs?page=roles).
- If you see Fix work but not **Accept**, **Enter value** or **Take it**, your role approves but does not fix. If you see the values but not **Not an issue**, your role fixes but does not approve.

sections.heading: I cannot approve my own batch
sections.text: "The batch creator cannot approve it" and "The batch creator cannot export it" are the four-eyes rule at work. Your decisions go into your own draft batch, and a second person with the approve permission must approve it. Ask your data owner or another steward. See [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals).

sections.heading: A value I sent still fails
sections.text:
The record panel reads "This value was sent to SAP, but the latest run still finds the record failing. Check the load, or propose another value." The record is back on **To fix**.

1. Check that the exported file was loaded into SAP, completely and into the right client. The batch's **Exported files** list gives each file's fingerprint.
2. Check that the run you are viewing finished after the load. Only runs that finish after the export reconcile.
3. If the load went in, read the issue's instruction and **Why it matters** again: the value may pass one rule and fail another, or SAP may have overwritten it. Enter another value, and it goes through approval again.
4. If the same records keep coming back, look at **Problems that come back** on [Progress](/docs?page=progress): the cause is probably upstream.

sections.heading: My records list is empty
sections.text: "Nothing left to fix" means every failing record in the run has a decision. "No records match these filters" means a filter hides them: select **Clear filters**. Check the **Status** filter too; it shows **Still open** records by default.

sections.heading: The fix sheet will not import
sections.text: Meridian reads only a sheet it exported. "No 'Fix sheet' sheet" or "The sheet's columns were changed" means the file was built by hand or its headers were edited: download a fresh fix sheet. Rows are skipped, and listed, when the **Decision** is not `fix`, `not an issue` or `accept risk`, when a sign-off has no **Reason**, or when the record no longer fails in the run. A file holds at most 5,000 decisions and 25 MB.

sections.heading: A system shows Unreachable or Sign-in refused
sections.text: Open the system's **Health** tab and select **Test connection**. **Unreachable** means the server could not reach SAP: check with your network or SAP team. **Sign-in refused** means SAP rejected the user: someone who manages systems updates the credentials.

sections.heading: A run failed
sections.text: Open the run from **Runs** and choose **Steps**. Each step shows its status, duration and error. Fix the cause, then select **Re-run analysis**. A run that stays running for a long time usually means the background workers have stopped: a server administrator checks them with `docker compose ps worker` and restarts them with `docker compose restart worker`.

sections.heading: The score looks capped
sections.text: One critical rule failing over tolerance caps an object at 85, two or more at 70. Work the critical records first: in Fix work, select the **Critical** figure.

sections.heading: How to report a problem
sections.text: Open the help menu (**?**), choose **Report a problem**, select **Copy details** and paste them into an email to the support address the dialog shows. The details are the page address, the run and the Meridian version. Nothing is sent from the dialog itself.

chapters.title: Glossary
chapters.summary: The words Meridian uses with a specific meaning, in alphabetical order. Each entry links to the chapter that explains it in full.

sections.text:
The words Meridian uses with a specific meaning, in alphabetical order. Each entry links to the chapter that explains it in full.

### Accept risk

A sign-off for a record that is wrong but acceptable for now, such as a value the business will correct later. Like **Not an issue**, it needs a reason, which is kept in the record's history, and the approve permission. The record then reads **Not an issue**. See [Fix work](/docs?page=fix).

### Applicability

Whether a rule applies to a system. Once the system's configuration is loaded, each rule is checked against it. **Applies** means the configuration uses the field. **Does not apply** means it does not, so the rule is skipped. **Applies by default** means no configuration is loaded yet. **Not available** means the system cannot supply what the rule needs. See [Rules](/docs?page=rules).

### Approved

The status of a record whose value sits in a fix batch a second person has approved. It waits to be exported for the SAP load. See [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals).

### Baseline

The run you pin as the reference for later runs from the same source, such as the run before a cleansing project. Each lineage has at most one. Comparisons use the baseline when there is one, and the previous run otherwise. See [Analysis](/docs?page=analysis).

### Basis

What a figure is measured against: which rules were counted, which records they ran over and which run produced them. A percentage only means something with its basis. Rules that do not apply to your configuration are left out of the basis rather than counted as passes. See [Rules](/docs?page=rules).

### Blocking rule

A failing rule that stands in the way of a Go verdict. On Home and on object pages it is a failing rule of critical or high severity. The readiness views count failing critical rules and the rules the S/4HANA readiness rule map marks as blocking. Also called a blocker. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Cadence

How often an object is checked by itself, such as daily at 02:00, or manual only when nobody scheduled it. Freshness is judged against it. See [Monitoring](/docs?page=monitoring).

### Cap

A ceiling on an object's score when critical rules fail. One critical rule over tolerance caps the score at 85; two or more cap it at 70. The score shows the capped value, the measured value beyond it and the rules that caused the cap, so you can see what to fix to lift it. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Confidence

How sure Meridian is that a proposed fix is right: **High**, **Medium** or **Low**. A high-confidence proposal from a rule has been checked by running the rule again on the new value. An approver can accept all high-confidence proposals in a batch at once. See [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals).

### Conformance

How closely the cases found by process discovery follow the intended process model. Each case is replayed against the model to find skipped steps, extra steps and steps in the wrong order. It is summarised as fitness and listed per step. See [Analysis](/docs?page=analysis).

### Contract

A data contract: an agreed quality level for a set of data, such as a minimum score or a maximum number of failing records. It is checked after every run and marked met or breached. A breach notifies the owner. See [Rules](/docs?page=rules).

### Critical tolerance

How much a critical rule may fail before it caps the score. By default a failing critical rule caps the score when it fails on at least 0.1% of the records it checked, or on at least 25 records. The tolerance is set per tenant. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Data quality score (DQS)

A score from 0 to 100 for how fit the data is. It is built from record-level pass rates, scaled by severity, averaged per dimension and then weighted across the six dimensions: completeness and accuracy 25% each, consistency 20%, and timeliness, uniqueness and validity 10% each. The weights are configurable per tenant. Failing critical rules can cap it. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Dimension

One of the six ways data quality is measured, from DAMA DMBOK. Completeness asks whether values are present, accuracy whether they are right, consistency whether related values and systems agree, timeliness whether data is current, uniqueness whether records repeat, and validity whether values follow the format. Every rule belongs to one dimension. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Draft batch

Your own fix batch that collects every value you accept or enter in Fix work, named "Fixes by" and your name. It is created on your first decision and stays a draft until a second person approves it. See [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals).

### Drift

A change in configuration or in how data behaves since it was last read, such as a field that turned from optional to required. Each drift entry names what changed and when, so a change in the score can be traced to a change in SAP rather than to the data. See [Data in](/docs?page=data-in).

### Dry run

A trial load that shows what the target system would reject, without changing anything. The target's own checks are applied to the source records and the blocked records are listed with the reason. See [Data in](/docs?page=data-in).

### Field status

Whether a field is required, optional, display only or suppressed in your SAP configuration. Meridian reads it from the configuration to decide whether an empty value is a defect. A required field that is empty fails; a suppressed one is not expected to hold data. See [Data in](/docs?page=data-in).

### Finding

The result of one rule in one run: how many records the rule checked, how many failed and which ones. A failing finding lists its records, why it matters and how to fix it. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Fitness

A measure from 0 to 1 of how many discovered process cases can be replayed on the reference model without deviation. It is 1 when every case fits exactly and falls as cases skip, repeat or reorder steps. See [Analysis](/docs?page=analysis).

### Fix batch

A set of record-level corrections approved and exported together. A second person must approve it: the person who drafted the batch cannot approve or export it. The export is a file, such as a Migration Cockpit workbook or a mass change file, that you load into SAP through your own process. On the next run each record is marked **Fixed** or **Still failing**. See [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals).

### Fix proposed

The status of a record whose value waits in a draft fix batch for a second person to approve. **Undo** takes the value back out. See [Fix work](/docs?page=fix).

### Fix sheet

An Excel workbook of the filtered work list, one row per record and failing check, with blank **New value**, **Decision** and **Reason** columns. Fill it in offline and import it back; each row becomes a decision in your draft batch. See [Fix work](/docs?page=fix).

### Fixed

The status of a record a later run showed passing. Only a run can mark a record fixed, so the count always reflects what SAP now holds. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Four eyes

The rule that two people handle every fix: one decides the value, another approves the batch. The person who drafted a batch cannot approve or export it. See [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals).

### Freshness

Whether an object has been checked as often as its cadence promises: Fresh, Due, Stale, Failed, Paused or Manual. Stale means older than one and a half times the cadence. See [Monitoring](/docs?page=monitoring).

### Ghost configuration

Configuration that exists in SAP but is never used in a transaction, such as a payment term or a plant that no document refers to. It adds noise to checks and choices to users. The list helps you decide what to retire before a migration. See [Data in](/docs?page=data-in).

### Golden record

The single best version of a business partner, material or other entity, assembled from matching records across systems. Survivorship rules pick each field's value. The golden record links back to every source record, so a change can be traced. See [Master data](/docs?page=mdm).

### Grain

The level a rule judges at, such as a header row, a line item or a document. Counting at the right grain keeps the pass rate honest: one purchase order with five bad lines is one failing document and five failing lines. See [Rules](/docs?page=rules).

### Grant

A role given to a user in addition to their main role, for all systems, for one system, for one object, or for one object on one system. A grant adds rights only where it applies. See [Roles and access](/docs?page=roles).

### Happy path

The most common route through a process, ideally the one the design intended. Its share of all cases shows how standard the process really is. See [Analysis](/docs?page=analysis).

### Impact

A number that ranks the work: the failing records of a rule multiplied by a severity weight of 8 for critical, 4 for high, 2 for medium and 1 for low. It is a ranking, not a sum of money. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Issue

One rule that one record fails. A record can have several issues. In Fix work the **Issues** list groups them by rule, so you can work one problem across many records. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Lineage

The chain of runs that come from the same source and may be compared. Runs extracted from a system belong to that system's lineage. Imported files are grouped by the objects they carry. Trends and comparisons never cross lineages. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Match rule

A rule that scores how likely two records describe the same real-world entity. It compares chosen fields, exactly or fuzzily, and gives each pair a confidence between 0 and 1. Pairs above the automatic merge threshold are merged, pairs in the review band go to a steward, and pairs below it are left alone. See [Master data](/docs?page=mdm).

### Not an issue

The status of a record someone signed off as an exception, with a reason: the value is right for the business even though the rule flags it. It needs the approve permission and can be withdrawn. See [Fix work](/docs?page=fix).

### Object

One area of SAP data that Meridian measures as a whole, such as Material master, Business partner or FI general ledger. Each object has its own rules, score and verdict. See [Objects](/docs?page=objects).

### Pass rate

The share of the records a rule checked that passed, from 0 to 100. Every score in Meridian is built from pass rates, so a rule failing on one record in a million barely moves the score. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Population exclusion

Records a rule deliberately skips, such as a vendor already flagged for deletion. Excluded records are neither passes nor failures, and the exclusion is listed with the rule so it can be reviewed. See [Rules](/docs?page=rules).

### Proven cost

Money measured on documents actually posted in SAP with a defective value, such as a payment sent twice. It is shown per top-level process in the tenant currency and is never added up across processes. See [Analysis](/docs?page=analysis).

### Readiness verdict

Whether an object is ready to use or load: **Go** when the score meets the target and no critical rule is over tolerance, **At risk** when the score is at or above the warning threshold, and **No-go** below it. Reports call At risk "conditional". See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Record

One row a rule judges, such as one material, one vendor or one sales order line. Each record is identified by its record key. See [Objects](/docs?page=objects).

### Record key

The SAP key fields that identify a record, such as the material number, written as `MATNR=...`. Type a record key in search to jump to the record. See [Objects](/docs?page=objects).

### Role

The set of rights a user holds, such as Data steward, Analyst or Viewer. Every user has one main role, and may hold more through grants. See [Roles and access](/docs?page=roles).

### Root cause

Whether a failure comes from bad data, bad configuration or both. A mistyped value is a data problem; a field that the rule treats as mandatory but SAP does not is a configuration problem. Knowing which sends the fix to the right team. See [Objects](/docs?page=objects).

### Rule

One fixed, deterministic check on the data, with an ID such as `MM001`, a dimension, a severity and a grain. The same data always gives the same result. See [Rules](/docs?page=rules).

### Run

One measurement of your data at a point in time, created by an extraction from a system or by an imported file. Every score, finding and record list belongs to a run. See [Analysis](/docs?page=analysis).

### Scope

The systems, objects and records a figure or a grant covers. A figure shown for a scope is not a total for the whole installation. A scoped grant gives a role for one system, one object or both. See [Roles and access](/docs?page=roles).

### Score band

The range a score falls in, set by three thresholds. By default 90 or more meets the target, 75 to below 90 is a warning, below 75 fails, and below 60 is the critical band. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Sent to SAP

The status of a record whose batch was exported for the SAP load. The next run confirms the fix: the record becomes **Fixed**, or goes back to **To fix** if it still fails. See [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals).

### Severity

How much a rule's failure matters: critical, high, medium or low. Severity changes how a failure counts in the score, in the cap, in blocking and in impact. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Steward

The person who looks after the data in an area and fixes its failing records. Stewards work from Fix work and the Inbox. Data steward is also a role in Meridian, and stewards land on Fix work after sign-in. See [Roles and access](/docs?page=roles).

### Still failing

A record that was sent to SAP but that the next run still finds failing. It returns to **To fix** with a warning, and its batch item reads **Still failing**. See [Troubleshooting](/docs?page=troubleshooting).

### Suggestion

The value Meridian proposes for a failing field: the rule's own fix, checked by running the rule again on the new value, the rule's fixed mapping for a known bad value, or a cleaning engine proposal with its confidence. Accept it with one click or the `a` key. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Survivorship

The rules that choose, field by field, which source value a golden record keeps when sources disagree: for example the most recent, the most complete, the trusted system or the most frequent. Rules suggested by the AI take effect only once a person activates them. See [Master data](/docs?page=mdm).

### To do

The ranked list of what needs a person now in your scope, opened from the flag in the index bar. Each item has one button that opens its fix. See [To do](/docs?page=todo).

### To fix

The status of a failing record nobody has decided a value for yet. It is open work, together with **Fix proposed**, **Approved** and **Sent to SAP**. See [Key concepts](/docs?page=concepts).

### Unmaintained field

A field that exists in SAP but is almost never filled in. It usually means the field is no longer part of the business process. Meridian lists these so you can retire the field or the rule that checks it. See [Data in](/docs?page=data-in).

### Value at risk

A money figure for SAP features blocked by bad data: the number of affected records multiplied by the value per record your organisation sets for that feature. It is shown per top-level business process in the tenant currency, never added up across processes. A feature nobody has priced shows no value. See [Analysis](/docs?page=analysis).

### Variant

A distinct path that cases take through a process. Cases with the same sequence of steps form one variant. Many rare variants point to rework, workarounds or steps done out of order. See [Analysis](/docs?page=analysis).

### Wave

A batch of objects and systems migrated together in one cutover, with one verdict: Go when it meets its minimum readiness, At risk when close, and No-go when blocking records remain. See [Data in](/docs?page=data-in).

### Work list

The failing records of one run, ranked worst first with their statuses, built as part of every analysis. Fix work and each object's **Records to fix** tab read it. See [Fix work](/docs?page=fix).

### Write-back

Sending an approved change straight into SAP instead of exporting a file, offered as **Write back** on a golden record. Someone other than the requester must approve each request, under **Approvals** in the Inbox, beside the fix batches. A deployment can switch live write-back off; you then export fixes as a file and load them in SAP. See [Approvals and export](/docs?page=approvals).

### Z-object

A customer-defined table, field or program in SAP, named with a Z or Y prefix. Meridian finds them, lists who owns them and whether they are documented, and flags unusual values in them. See [Data in](/docs?page=data-in).

sections.heading: Numbers on screen
sections.text:
Every number Meridian shows has one name and one meaning, listed here in the order they appear in the product.

### Score

The data quality score of the object or run, from 0 to 100, held down when a critical rule fails.

### Verdict

Go, At risk or No-go, from the score and your score bands.

### Failing rules

Rules that failed on at least one record in the run.

### Critical and high failing rules

Failing rules of critical or high severity, the ones that stand in the way of a Go verdict.

### Rule failures

Failing records summed over every failing rule: a record failing two rules counts twice.

### Records to fix

Distinct records in the work list that still need a decision, however many rules they fail.

### Critical records

Records to fix whose worst failing rule is critical.

### With a suggested value

Records to fix that already carry a suggested value you can accept.

### Overdue records

Records to fix that are past their due date.

### Approvals waiting

Fix batches and SAP write-backs that wait for a second person to approve.

### Open inbox items

Inbox items that are open, in progress or escalated.

### Overdue inbox items

Open inbox items that are past their due time.

### Objects below target

Objects whose verdict is At risk or No-go.

### New failing records

Records that fail in this run and passed in the baseline.

### Recovered records

Records that failed in the baseline and pass now.

### Newly failing rules

Rules that fail now and did not fail in the baseline.

### Recovered rules

Rules that failed in the baseline and have no failures now.
